req.title: Login required for create
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they attempt GET /create.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-012 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users who attempt GET /create are redirected to /auth/login with a 302 status. The violation was that test[0] had kind=negative but heuristic=EP. EP (Equivalence Partitioning) is a positive-class heuristic when applied to the valid partition; however, the anonymous-user redirect IS the primary specified behaviour (the requirement's main statement), so it is correctly classified as kind=positive with heuristic=EP (testing the nominal/specified partition). Fixed: test[0] kind changed from 'negative' to 'positive'. Three test cases: (1) Positive/EP — anonymous GET /create yields exactly 302 to /auth/login (the primary requirement). (2) Negative/NEG — authenticated user GET /create yields 200, not a redirect (catches boolean-negation mutation on login_required guard). (3) Boundary/STC — state transition: login then logout then GET /create must redirect again (catches mutations that leave session state dirty after logout).

tests.name: test_anonymous_get_create_redirects_to_login
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database
No user is logged in (no session cookie)
actions: Send GET /create with no session cookie
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/create')
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
location = r.headers.get('Location', '')
assert location == '/auth/login', f'Expected /auth/login, got {location!r}'

tests.name: test_authenticated_get_create_returns_200
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database seeded with pre-loaded users
User Rahul (id=1, password=stone) exists in the database
User is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: Send GET /create with the authenticated session
expected: Login response status code is exactly 302
GET /create response status code is exactly 200
Response body contains the create form (not a redirect)
trace: Catches boolean-negation mutation on login_required guard
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert login_r.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {login_r.status_code}'
r = client.get('/create')
assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 for authed user, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers.get('Location', '') != '/auth/login', 'Authenticated user should not be redirected to login'

tests.name: test_logout_then_get_create_redirects_again
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database seeded with pre-loaded users
User Anjali (id=2, password=cloud) exists in the database
User logs in, then logs out, then attempts GET /create
expected: Second GET /create Location header is exactly /auth/login
trace: R-FLASKR-012: state transition anonymous→authenticated→anonymous; second GET /create must redirect
Catches mutations that leave session state dirty after logout
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
assert login_r.status_code == 302
r1 = client.get('/create')
assert r1.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 while logged in, got {r1.status_code}'
logout_r = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert logout_r.status_code == 302
r2 = client.get('/create')
assert r2.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 after logout, got {r2.status_code}'
location = r2.headers.get('Location', '')
assert location == '/auth/login', f'Expected /auth/login, got {location!r}'
